However, the source also asserts qualitative sharpness of the entire tail, a smallest-tail-value comparison, and negligibility of sqrt(2 pi k); those claims are not present in the target proposition, and the source does not define the standard of approximation. It is therefore unclear whether the proposition alone entails the selected remark in full.

rationale: The target reproduces every term in display (2.9) correctly and gives the standard fixed-positive-rate Stirling interpretation as asymptotic equivalence when k tends to infinity. The rendered source, however, leaves the approximation sign, error notion, parameter regime, and zero-rate boundary unstated, while the selected remark also contains qualitative tail-sharpness conclusions absent from the proposition. These are substantive unresolved semantic choices rather than harmless notation. Both implication directions are therefore unclear, the classification is undetermined, acceptance is false, and fresh adjudication is required.
